newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Iranians pelt German embassy, France warns Tehran.
newsitem.headline: Iranians pelt German embassy, France warns Tehran.

text.p: Hundreds of slogan-chanting Iranians pelted the German embassy in Tehran with tomatoes on Friday while most European Union states summoned home their envoys in a deepening row over political slayings in Europe.

EU members, with the exception of Greece, recalled their envoys for consultations following Thursday's German court verdict that Iran's rulers ordered the killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

Athens said it had expressed its reservations about the EU's appeal to member states to withdraw their envoys from Tehran. It said it was opposed to terrorism and the use of violence but found that isolating a country was not the best way to bring it into the international community.
The German court decision forced the EU to abandon its controversial "critical dialogue" in a move which delighted the United States and other opponents of Tehran's radical Islamic government.
The German Foreign Ministry thanked its EU partners for the show of solidarity while Paris warned Tehran to avoid any violent backlash against German of European interests.
"France's solidarity with Germany is total in this matter," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt declared, adding:
"In the immediate future, France is particularly attentive to the measures which Iran takes to prevent any inappropriate reaction towards German or European nationals or interests."

In Tehran -- witnesses said demonstators, who had marched four km (2.5 miles) from Friday's mass prayers at Tehran university -- rushed a line of riot police behind barricades at the embassy, but were pushed back.

Witnesses said the protesters, many members of a hardline Islamist group, chanted "Death to Germany" and "Fascist Germany, servant of Zionism", in addition to the familiar "Death to America" and "Death to Israel" slogans.
Iran's president sought to play down the dispute, saying the the diplomatic row was a "passing storm" provoked by the United States and Israel.

"The (U.S. and Israel) needed such a propaganda wave. We should expect them to keep up the noise in the West. But this will bring them nothing. It is like a thunderstorm that brings clear weather in its wake," Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, a Shi'ite Moslem cleric, said in his Friday prayers address.
The United States, which has long argued that Europe is motivated by commercial greed for deals in Iran, applauded the suspension of critical dialogue which it says is fruitless.

Iran has been a major bone of contention between Washington and its European allies. The EU has refused to join U.S. trade sanctions on Iran and has attacked U.S. legislation cracking down on firms that invest in the oil or gas industry there.

"We hope the European Union will join the United States in a realistic policy that is aimed at containing Iran and containing its ability to further destabilise the Middle East and to murder its own citizens abroad," the United States said on Thursday.
Tehran denies that it supports terrorism.
Non-EU member Norway, which severed relations with Tehran almost two years ago, called on the European Union to back the United States and consider imposing trade sanctions on Iran.
A foreign ministry spokesman said the appeal from Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal was made in a meeting with EU ambassadors in Oslo.
Supporters of death threat author Salman Rushdie also welcomed the decision to withdraw ambassadors from Iran.

"We are very pleased that the efforts to silence the German prosecutors have not worked. Terrorism in Europe perpetrated by Iran has been going on for many, many years," Frances D'Souza of the international Rushdie defence committee told Reuters.
Iran's late spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomenei ordered Rushdie's killing in 1989 following publication of his novel "The Satanic Verses" which was deemed blasphemous to Islam.

Germany, Iran's largest trading partner and most important Western friend, ordered four Iranian diplomats to leave the country and recalled its ambassador in Tehran immediately after the court verdict.
